label: claim-wider-than-code
name: A sentence in the body, a Note, a spec or a file header promises more subjects, paths or defaults than the code enforces or measures
description: What breaks: the text covers an 'or', a plural, 'every' or a default that only one path or one literal honors. native_k_view is a using alias, so 'a bare pointer is a compile error' holds for V only (4188336267, check 6 as written); join_wait_cycles is documented as ending when an FPGA pass or the software partials become ready, but only the hardware join is timed, so the body's sample value 0 comes from the untimed path (4125033634 'That spin is never timed'); the spec says a pool holds 'one or more chunks' while heap_start reads chunks[0] (3227529208 'So is the spec wrong? Or are these functions insufficient?'); the file header says 'default ON' while the #ifndef fallback still says 0 after the CMake default moved (3501641254). Also the PR 3490 body calling a runtron flag a 'Perfetto option' (5106398334 part 1, counted under observability). Procedure (check 6 widened): extract every subject a sentence covers (each type, each 'or' path, each plural, each default, each component name) and trace each to the code line that reaches the enforcement or measurement; for every timer or counter list the paths its doc names and verify start/stop executes on each; for every changed default grep every literal bound to the same setting name. Offer both repairs: change the code, or narrow the text.
disposition_reason: Check 6 triggers only on compile-time rejection sentences; the corpus widens the subject to timers, specs with plural subjects and stated defaults.
agent_feasibility: yes: extract plural/or/every subjects and trace each to a code path; grep literals bound to a changed default.

members.concern: The join-wait timer T5 (join_wait_cycles) is only measured inside the hardware join (stream_hw_joins), while the software-only join's poll loop in run_joins is never timed, so the documented meaning (ends when an FPGA pass or the other workers' partials become ready) is wider than what the code measures and the sample value 0 in the PR body comes from the untimed path.

detection.trigger: The diff adds a timer or counter at one site and a Note, README or PR-body sentence describes it with an 'or' / 'both' / 'every' subject (e.g. 'ends when a hardware pass or the software partials become ready').
detection.procedure: Expand the sentence's subjects. For each subject find the code path that produces it (grep the branch variable, e.g. `join_hw`, `!join_hw`, `continue;  // poll`, in the file at HEAD) and check whether the rdtsc start/stop or the counter increment is executed on that path. Also read any sample output in the PR body: a 0 under a configuration where the subject must be nonzero (CPU attention with several workers) confirms the gap.
detection.question: For every path the doc sentence names, does the timer's start and stop (or the counter increment) actually execute on that path?

members.quote: That spin is never timed. So on a CPU-attention run `join_wait_cycles` reads 0 even when workers are spinning on load imbalance; the `"join_wait_cycles":0` in the PR description's sample comes from exactly that config.
members.note: Verified at 1430736b2a: self_attention.hpp:1258 `if (!join_hw && plan_state.sections_left[kv_head]) continue;  // poll` has no rdtsc around it; README.stats.md:260 describes T5 for both joins. Wade's finding shape: fact (only timed here), consequence ('So ... reads 0'), doc contradiction, then two remedies (time the SW poll too, or narrow the docs). Author fixed by timing the software poll (commit 'T5 covers the software-only join (review round 4, W1)'). Check 6 as written fires only on type-safety 'cannot be passed' claims; the theme (claim wider than enforcement) matches, the trigger does not.

members.concern: native_k_view is only a `using` alias of the generic row-major view, and the test asserts it is constructible from const bf16*, so the PR-body guarantee 'a bare pointer is a compile error' holds for the V plane only; state that in the description and give K a distinct type in the child PR #4424.

detection.trigger: A PR-body, commit, Note or comment sentence says an input is rejected at compile time ('bare pointer is a compile error', 'cannot be passed') for a plural or 'and'-joined set of subjects, and the diff introduces a `using` alias (not a new class) for one of those subjects.
detection.procedure: for each subject in the claim, find the kernel parameter type in the diff, resolve it through every `using` to the defining template (view<...> in view.hpp); grep the tests for std::is_constructible_v on that alias from a pointer; grade: bare pointer at the call rejected (explicit ctor), wrapped pointer rejected (private/absent ctor), nominally distinct from any same-shaped view (new class). Compare each grade with the claim's wording.
detection.question: For every subject the guarantee sentence covers, which enforcement level does the code actually reach, and does the sentence say so?

members.quote: `native_k_view` is an alias of the generic row-major `view`, and t_llama_unit asserts it is constructible from `const bf16*`. So any pointer or row-major 64x128 bf16 view passes the QK kernel; "a bare pointer is a compile error" holds for V only.
members.note: Verified at c5d44bd86f: h/tron/tensor/kv_cache_fwd.hpp:42-47 `using native_k_view = view<bf16, VIEW_ALIGNED_TRUE, VIEW_DMA_FALSE, ...>`; t/t_llama_unit.cpp has `STATIC_REQUIRE(std::is_constructible_v<k_plane_t, const bf16*>)`. Qualification from references/pr4557-misses.md: the view's pointer ctor is explicit (view.hpp:296), so a bare pointer at the call is still rejected for K; what passes is a pointer wrapped in one expression or any same-shaped view. Severity wording 'Fine as a first step'. Author narrowed the Short version and the #4424 table; a distinct K type deferred to #4424.

members.concern: Asks whether the `#ifndef` fallback `#define TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON 0` at line 72 of src/system/memory.cpp should also become 1, now that the CMake option default is ON and the file's header comment says 'default ON'.

detection.trigger: the diff changes a default value or a comment stating a default (CMake option(), env default, config literal) and the same file or its consumers hold another literal for the same setting (a `#ifndef X / #define X <value>` fallback, a duplicated constant, a doc table)
detection.procedure: take the option or macro name from the hunk; grep the whole file and the repo (`grep -rn TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON src/ h/ doc/ CMakeLists.txt`) for every other literal bound to that name; for each hit decide from the CMake add_compile_definitions line whether the build always defines the macro (then the fallback is the option-OFF path) or not (then the fallback is the real default)
detection.question: does every literal bound to this setting name now agree with the new default, and for each one that differs, is it a deliberate fallback for a different build path?

members.quote: would it make sense to flip this to 1 at the same time, to make things consistent?
members.note: Verified at commit 6590b12915: memory.cpp lines 66-72 read '#ifndef TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON / #define TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON 0 / #endif' and read_arena_allocator_env() returns `TRON_ARENA_ALLOCATOR_DEFAULT_ON != 0` when the env var is unset. The comment was posted on an unchanged line (+72) via Graphite, so Wade read beyond the hunk. Author explained the 0 is the option-OFF fallback (CMake passes -D...=1 when the option is ON) and it should stay; Wade approved 7 minutes later at the same commit. Skill check 6 shares the theme (stated default vs declaration) but its trigger is limited to compile-time rejection claims about parameter types.

members.concern: The design spec says a pool can hold 'one or more chunks', but heap_start() and heap_size() (the functions that report the DMA heap range to the driver) read only pool.chunks[0]; Wade asks whether the spec is wrong or the functions are insufficient, noting expand() called twice would create more than one chunk.

detection.trigger: Production code indexes a collection with a fixed index ([0], .front(), .back()) or asserts non-empty only, while a design doc, Note or comment in the same PR says the collection can hold several elements.
detection.procedure: For each added `x[0]` / `.front()` / `.chunks.empty()` guard on a container, grep the PR's doc/*.md, Notes and header comments for the container's cardinality ('one or more', 'multiple', 'list of'); find every caller that can grow the container (here expand()) and count its call sites; if the doc allows N and the code handles 1, ask which is right and request an assert or a doc fix.
detection.question: If the container ever holds more than one element, is this read still correct, and if not, does an assert or the doc say that only one is allowed?

members.quote:
the spec says a pool can have "one or more chunks"... but we only ever look at `chunks[0]` here and below in heap_size. So is the spec wrong? Or are these functions insufficient?

If `expand()` is called multiple times, we would create >1 chunk right?
members.note: Wade cross-read doc/pos_heap_v2.md ('mmap that budget as one or more chunks') against the code. The hunk showed `TRON_ASSERT(!h->pool.chunks.empty(), ...)` then `return h->pool.chunks[0].base`. Commit e4c4f49452 replaced the non-empty assert with `TRON_ASSERT_EQ(h->pool.chunks.size(), 1u)` in both heap_start and heap_size and added a comment explaining that internals support multi-chunk but the VFIO IOMMU map and dispatch surface assume one chunk.

codex_bullets.bullet: Map each counter or timer to all promised execution paths, including software-only, hardware, mixed, and alternate callers. A zero can mean an uninstrumented path rather than no work.
codex_bullets.reason: Three comments (PRs 4596, 2766). The 4596 review is the only counters PR in the corpus, so the count is low but the finding was his headline item there.

codex_bullets.bullet: Compare guarantees with enforcing declarations. Direct pointer rejection, explicit wrapping, distinct types, alignment, ownership, and lifetime are separate properties. Narrow an overclaim without inventing a stronger implementation requirement.
codex_bullets.reason: One comment (PR 4557). Claude check 6 grades the three levels.

codex_bullets.bullet: Lead with the concrete fact at a HEAD location. State the consequence and the smallest supported remedy.
codex_bullets.reason: Three comments (PRs 4557, 4596) in the fact / consequence / ask shape. The Claude skill already describes this shape.

codex_bullets.bullet: For a design question, state the tradeoff and preserve a deliberate staged limitation.
codex_bullets.reason: Five comments (PRs 4596, 4557, 2777, 2176). Already in the Claude skill.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: covered (How Wade words: "A design concern is a question with two alternatives"; check 6: "preserve a deliberate staged limitation")

codex_bullets.bullet: For every metric, write its unit and scope, then locate all writers and readers. Check software, hardware, mixed, and alternate entry paths. Trace reset, begin, end, aggregation, and publication. Check row identity stays stable when workers change roles. Verify trace categories and event rates fit the capture buffer.
codex_bullets.reason: Five comments (PRs 4596, 2287, 3016), plus 3406007619 on atomics for the FUSE reader thread. Procedure form of C22, C23, C25; adopt as one instrumentation check.

codex_bullets.bullet: If the code measures a narrower scope than the documentation promises, offer either implementing the missing measurement or narrowing the claim. Do not require a new instrumentation design when the author explicitly accepts the narrower scope.
codex_bullets.reason: Two comments (PR 4596). The both-repairs rule is already in the Claude skill; the second sentence is author-side guidance from the 4596 round.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: partial (How Wade words: "Every text-versus-code mismatch offers both repairs")

codex_bullets.reason: One comment (PR 4557). Claude check 6 has the same three levels.
